trial_court: Joint District Judge, Kachchh at Gandhidham, Regular Civil Appeal No. 189 of 1999
case_name: Jagdish Mangtani vs Geeta Jagdish Mangtani
facts_of_case: Marriage between Jagdish and Geeta was solemnised on 2-11-1993. The husband worked in a shop for Rs. 1400/- per month while the wife served as primary teacher at Adipur, drawing salary of Rs. 7000/- per month. After marriage, the wife took leave and came to Ulhasnagar, Mumbai, but later proposed settling at Adipur. The husband did not agree, leading to disputes and quarrels.

legal_principles.principle: Desertion to amount to a matrimonial offence must be for a continuous period of not less than two years immediately preceding the presentation of the petition.
legal_principles.held: This clause has to be read with the Explanation. The Explanation has widened the definition of desertion to include 'wilful neglect' of the petitioning spouse by the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: Two essential conditions must be there for the offence of desertion: (1) the factum of separation, and (2) the intention to bring cohabitation permanently to an end.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, for the offence of desertion, so far as the deserting spouse is concerned, two essential conditions must be there, namely, (1) the factum of separation, and (2) the intention to bring cohabitation permanently to an end.
keywords: intention to bring cohabitation permanently to an end

legal_principles.principle: For the offence of desertion, two essential elements are essential so far as the deserted spouse is concerned: (1) absence of consent, and (2) intention to bring cohabitation permanently to an end.
legal_principles.held: Similarly, two elements are essential so far as the deserted spouse is concerned : (1) absence of consent, and (2) intention to bring cohabitation permanently to an end.
keywords: intention to bring cohabitation permanently to an end

legal_principles.principle: The legislature intended to give the expression 'desertion' a wide import which includes wilful neglect of the petitioner by the other party to the marriage.
legal_principles.held: From the Explanation it is abundantly clear that the legislature intended to give to the expression a wide import which includes wilful neglect of the petitioner by the other party to the marriage.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's judgment and decree dated 18-6-1999 passed by the learned Civil Judge (S.D.), Gandhidham, in Hindu Marriage Petition No. 14 of 1998 was quashed and set aside.
